identification: Set of 10 Murano (Venetian) vaseline/uranium glass stemware, c.1920s-50s: 3 coupes (champagne/cocktail) with spiral-ribbed pale yellow-green uranium bowl and foot and a pink/rose aventurine (gold-fleck) dolphin stem with black-dot eyes on a uranium knop; and 7 tall conical goblets/vases in pale green uranium glass with a gold-foil (aventurine) ribbed knop and plain foot. Coupe glows bright green under UV in photo 2; goblet glows in photo 3. This dolphin-stem coupe form is the classic Salviati/Venice & Murano Glass Co type and was made by several Murano firms (Salviati, Cenedese, Toso). Unmarked, which is normal for Salviati table glass (paper labels only). So: Salviati-TYPE Murano, not provable as Salviati.
marks_seen: None visible in the 3 photos (no acid stamp, no label). UV glow confirmed in photos 2 and 3.

identification: Rand McNally 'Star Chart for Southern Skies', edited by Dr. Oliver Justin Lee, Director of Dearborn Observatory, Northwestern University; 'Copyright by Rand McNally & Company, New York Chicago San Francisco, Made in U.S.A.' White-on-black polar star chart with month/date ring and magnitude legend. The design was copyrighted 1936-37 (Northern Skies 5 Jan 1937) and Lee was Dearborn director to 1947, so originals are c.1937-1947 (sellers call them 1940s). Two unframed sheets: one hung showing Southern Skies; the second is rolled underneath, title not visible (most likely the companion 'Star Chart for Northern Skies', unconfirmed). No date printed, no size in the catalogue. Originals were classroom wall charts about 45 x 45 in, often linen-backed on dowels; ours shows a white paper margin, a ring/grommet at top corner and a glossy surface, with no dowels seen, so it may be an unbacked school chart, a folding version, or a later reprint. Cannot settle from photos.
marks_seen: Title block and Rand McNally copyright line read; no copyright year visible; no size stated.
google_searches: '"Oliver Justin Lee" "star chart" rand mcnally'; '"star chart for southern skies"'; '"rand mcnally" "star chart" "southern skies" sold OR realized OR hammer'; 'rand mcnally "star chart for southern skies" reproduction OR reprint OR print poster'. Findings: Rand McNally registered 'Star chart for northern skies' copyright 5 Jan 1937 (Catalog of Copyright Entries on archive.org), so the pair dates from 1937 on; Lee was Dearborn director from 1930 to 1947, so original printings are c.1937-1947. Originals were classroom pull-down charts about 45 x 45 in, often linen-backed with dowels (WorthPoint listing 1906300789 description). Folding paper versions (Northern and Southern) also exist.

I found no new dated SOLD prices for this chart. eBay sold (90-day window, worldwide) has none; LiveAuctioneers and Invaluable have none; WorthPoint has several sold Rand McNally Northern/Southern Skies star charts (e.g. worthopedia 1906300789, 1915172741, 1832558052) but hides price and date without a subscription. The only price evidence besides the 2 single-bid US eBay sales behind the existing max is asking prices (US$500-1,200) from one Brooklyn seller, which have not sold. A$140 for both is reasonable IF they are originals, but nothing I found proves a market at that level, and reprint risk is real.

Check the back for linen backing, the paper type (old lithograph vs modern glossy print), and any printer's code or copyright year in the margins. Unroll the second sheet to confirm it is the Northern Skies companion. Check for tears, creases and losses.
